EDITION3_ART_DIRECTION

Edition 3 Art Direction — Visceral Grimdark Upgrade Brief

> **For `[Autarch Chronicler]` + `[Autarch Artist]`.** Elevate Edition 2 (current `docs/lore/VARN_FIELD_JOURNAL.pdf`) to a true 9.5+/10. Target: *Darkest Dungeon × Fear & Hunger × House of Leaves* field-journal spreads. No new systems — pure art direction & composition.

> **Auditor bar:** `docs/ART_QUALITY_AUDIT.md` (Skeptic, 9.5/10). Edition 2 Field Journal pages average ~8.0 — closest category to the bar, but still short on visceral ink density, marginalia integration, and crosshatch discipline.

  • --

    • 0. Global Rules for Edition 3 (apply to EVERY page)

    1. **Ink palette locked:** `#0e0b14` outer silhouette, `#382150` bone/sinew, `#6c4899` corroded splinters, `#ff32c8` rift/eye emissive ONLY. No washed-out greys, no clean whites.

    2. **Crosshatch discipline:** Diagonal pen-hatching **only inside shadows and recesses** (honoring `01-cel-style-guide.png`). Never on flat surfaces. Never parallel to the page edge.

    3. **Blood & soot density:** Every spread must contain **at least one** blood splatter, soot smear, or ash stain bleeding off the page edge. Pages should look recovered from a corpse, not printed.

    4. **Marginalia integration:** Every spread carries 1–3 handwritten marginal notes (Kael's voice, ≤ 55 chars, inked in a slightly different hand — pencil or thinner nib) placed in gutters, corners, or between columns. Notes must react to the illustration (e.g., "the spines face east — why?").

    5. **Paper tooth:** Aged parchment grain at 4% (`paper_grain.png`), with torn/ragged edges on at least 2 sides per page. No clean rectangular borders.

    6. **Locked pages (`page_locked`):** Must look *deliberately sealed*, not merely blank. Wax seal, torn corner, ink blot, and a single faded "??? — UNCHARTED" in Kael's hand. The lock should feel like a dare.

  • --

    • 1. Page-by-Page Critique & Upgrade Directives

    1.1 `entry_strata_depths` — "Beneath the Crust — The Four Strata"

  • *Current weakness:** Reads as a clean diagram. The radial cross-section is too tidy — straight layers, even spacing, no sense of compression or dread. Lacks the feeling of descending into something alive.
  • *Upgrade directives (Edition 3):**
  • **Composition:** Replace the clean radial diagram with a **vertical cross-section cut through the sphere** (like a geological core sample), tilted slightly so the layers read as strata pressing down. The top edge (surface) should be ragged, torn, ash-stained. The bottom edge (Core) should glow faintly amethyst through a crack in the basalt.
  • **Layer treatment:**
  • **Layer 0 (Surface & Shallow Crust, R=160→128):** Concrete foundations, buried metro bunkers, surface trenches — drawn as *ruins in cross-section*, not abstract blocks. Show a collapsed hab-block, a severed pipe, a buried sign.
  • **Layer 1 (Fractured Bedrock & Ore Strata, R=128→96):** Dense iron/alloy seams as **dark, jagged veins** splitting through cracked rock. Natural caverns as irregular voids. Trench Maw nests as dark spiral holes with teeth.
  • **Layer 2 (Deep Basalt & Abyssal Chasms, R=96→66):** High-grade amethyst crystal veins as **glowing magenta fractures** in black basalt. Ancient Autarch conduits as thin, pulsing lines. Claustrophobic caverns lit only by player-flare glow (a tiny cyan dot in the dark).
  • **Layer 3 (The Hollow Core Cavity, R=66→48):** The basalt ceiling should be **cracked and dripping**, with stalactites and magenta rift arcs. The Core City visible below as a glowing amethyst sphere, suspended in darkness, seen from above through the crack.
  • **Marginalia:** At least 3 notes: (a) "The basalt sings here. Do not whistle back." (b) "Layer 2 is where the drill starts to sweat." (c) "I heard something breathing in the crack. I did not look."
  • **Blood/soot:** Soot smear along the top edge (surface ash). A single blood drop falling from Layer 2 into Layer 3. The crack in the basalt should have dark, wet edges.
  • **Crosshatch:** Only inside the cavern voids and along the basalt cracks. Not on the crystal veins (those glow, they don't hatch).

    • 1.2 `entry_core_city` — "The Purple Crystalline Sphere City"

  • *Current weakness:** The Core City likely reads as a clean sci-fi render. It needs to be terrifying — a cathedral suspended in darkness, not a pretty gem.
  • *Upgrade directives (Edition 3):**
  • **Composition:** Drawn from **inside the hollow cavity, looking down at the inner sphere** (or from the surface of the inner sphere, looking up at the basalt ceiling). The `48 m` inner sphere should dominate the lower two-thirds of the spread. The basalt ceiling (with stalactites and rift arcs) should loom in the upper third.
  • **The city itself:** Jagged amethyst spires, rotating crystal rings (Core Warden's domain), weeping ink banners, and the Heart Citadel at the center — a colossal pulsating nexus with multi-phase horror waves implied (laser rifts, sky-hand slams) as faint, ominous silhouettes in the background.
  • **Lighting:** The only light sources are the city's own glow (amethyst) and the players' flares (tiny cyan dots at the edges). Everything else is darkness. The contrast should be extreme — bright crystal against pitch black.
  • **The 4 Spire Anchors:** Each should be drawn as a distinct, jagged pylon with a faint hum-line (sound-wave) emanating from it. The Four-Note Chord should be implied visually (4 small musical staff marks near each anchor, empty — for the player to fill in).
  • **Marginalia:** At least 3 notes: (a) "The city does not welcome. It endures." (b) "I counted four spires. The chord has four notes. I will not write the order." (c) "The Heart is not a heart. It is a mouth."
  • **Blood/soot:** A single blood trail leading from the edge of the inner sphere toward the Heart Citadel (a previous explorer's path). Soot on the basalt ceiling. Ink splatter where the Heart's pulse hits the page.
  • **Crosshatch:** Only on the basalt ceiling and the shadow sides of the spires. The crystal surfaces should be clean but cracked (fine line work, not hatching).

    • 1.3 `page_locked` — "??? — Uncharted"

  • *Current weakness:** Likely reads as a blank page with a lock icon. Needs to feel like a sealed, forbidden document — a dare.
  • *Upgrade directives (Edition 3):**
  • **Composition:** The page should be **visibly damaged** — torn corner (top-right), ink blot (bottom-left), wax seal (center, cracked, with a faint magenta glow seeping through the crack), and a faded "??? — UNCHARTED" in Kael's hand, slightly off-center.
  • **The wax seal:** Should be the focal point — a cracked crimson-magenta wax seal stamped with a symbol that is almost recognizable (a stylized eye? a crystal? a grid?). The crack in the seal should glow faintly, as if something is trying to get out.
  • **The ink blot:** Should be organic, spreading, as if the page was dropped in ink. It should partially obscure the "??? — UNCHARTED" text, making it harder to read — the lock is not just visual, it's physical.
  • **The torn corner:** Should reveal a sliver of the page beneath (a different color — darker, more saturated), implying that the locked page is layered over something else.
  • **Marginalia:** A single note, written in a different hand (pencil, thinner): "I do not know what is under this seal. I do not want to know. But I cannot stop looking."
  • **Blood/soot:** The wax seal should have a faint blood smear on its edge. The ink blot should have a soot halo.
  • **Crosshatch:** Only on the torn corner's exposed edge and the wax seal's shadow. The rest of the page should be clean parchment with the grain visible.
  • --

    • 2. Overall Density & Composition Upgrades

    2.1 Blood & Soot Density

  • **Minimum per spread:** 1 blood splatter (small, directional, with a tail) + 1 soot smear (broad, soft-edged) + 1 ash stain (fine, granular).
  • **Placement:** Blood should follow the action (near a wound, a death, a betrayal). Soot should follow the environment (near fire, near the Core, near industry). Ash should be everywhere — it's Varn.
  • **Color:** Blood = `#b82934` (crimson, not bright red). Soot = `#1d1a24` (deep ink, not grey). Ash = `#8a847b` (warm grey, fine).

    • 2.2 Crosshatch Density

  • **Target density:** 30–40% of any shadowed area should be hatched. Flat surfaces: 0%. Recesses/crevices: 60–70%.
  • **Direction:** Always diagonal (45° or 135°). Never horizontal or vertical. Never parallel to the page edge.
  • **Weight:** Outer silhouette = 4–6 px heavy ink. Inner detail = 1–2 px fine lines. Crosshatch = 0.5–1 px, spaced 2–3 px apart.

    • 2.3 Marginalia Composition

  • **Quantity:** 1–3 notes per spread. More than 3 clutters. Fewer than 1 feels empty.
  • **Placement:** Gutters (between columns), corners, or floating in negative space. Never over the main illustration.
  • **Hand:** Slightly different from Kael's main text — thinner nib, slightly smaller, slightly more hurried. Pencil for the most personal notes (fear, doubt). Ink for observations.
  • **Content:** Must react to the illustration. Not generic lore — specific, visceral, personal. "The spines face east — why?" not "The Hollow Stalker is dangerous."

    • 2.4 Page Edge Treatment

  • **Torn edges:** At least 2 sides per page (top and one side, or bottom and one side). Ragged, not clean.
  • **Staining:** Coffee/tea rings, ash smears, blood drops on at least 3 pages per chapter. These should be subtle — not the focus, but present.
  • **Wax/seal:** Only on locked pages and chapter dividers. The seal should be cracked, glowing faintly magenta.
  • --

    • 3. Edition 3 Page Priority List

    | Priority | Page | Current Score (est.) | Target | Key Fix |

    | 1 | `entry_strata_depths` | 7.0 | 9.5+ | Vertical cross-section, not clean radial diagram |

    | 7 | `cover_front` / `cover_back` | 8.0 | 9.5+ | Weathered leather, embossed title, blood/soot on edges |

  • [ ] Add blood/soot/ash density to all 27 pages per §2.1.

    • PHASE_B_CHRONICLE_DRAFTS

    Phase B Chronicle Drafts — Surveyor Kael's Field Notes

    > **Voice:** Surveyor M. Kael, lone doomed explorer charting Varn. Literature-grade grimdark (*Darkest Dungeon × Fear & Hunger × House of Leaves*). For `[Autarch Chronicler]` to illustrate and typeset. All entries encounter-gated.

  • --

    • Part I — Dead-Air Radio Transcripts (`surveyor_broadcast_01..07`)

    > One per biome. 40–65 words each. End in a cryptic coordinate/clue that pieces together the hidden pre-collapse bunker. Read aloud in Kael's voice, mono 24 kHz.

    01 — Ashen Ruins (The East March)

    > "Day forty-one. The Marches still smell of cordite and wet concrete. I found a rusted loudspeaker bolted to a hab-block roof, still humming on a dead frequency. It said one word, over and over, in a voice I almost recognized: *southwest*. The bunker is southwest. I am sure of it the way you are sure of a dream you cannot wake from. The ash here is warm. It should not be warm."

    02 — Shattered Wilds (The Broken Highway)

    > "Day fifty-three. The Wilds ate the highway whole. I tuned a cracked radio on a burnt-out truck and heard static, then a woman's voice reading numbers: seven, fourteen, twenty-two. Degrees south of the Seat. The bunker is at seven-fourteen-twenty-two. I wrote it on my palm. The ink bled through before I finished. The wilds do not want coordinates remembered."

    03 — Drowned Mire (The Sunken Basin)

    > "Day sixty. The Mire swallowed my boots and almost my nerve. A radio half-buried in silt played a recording of rain — but the rain was singing. Between the drops, a bearing: *ninety degrees east of the pole, where the water is shallowest.* I waded. The water was warm. The water is always warm here. I think the Mire is breathing."

    04 — Obsidian Wastes (The Black Glass)

    > "Day sixty-eight. The Wastes are loud. The basalt hums a note that gets under your teeth. A radio tower — the only thing standing — broadcast a single tone, then a man's voice: *the bunker lies where the lightning refuses to strike.* I watched the sky for an hour. One patch of ground, maybe forty metres across, never took a bolt. I marked it. The Wastes did not like being marked."

    05 — Scorched Salt Flats (The White Expanse)

    > "Day seventy-four. The Flats are blinding. The salt cuts your eyes and your memory. A radio half-melted into the crust hissed, then spoke: *walk until the mirage stops lying.* I walked. The mirage showed me the Keep I lost. Then it stopped. Past it, the ground cracked open and I saw concrete. The bunker is real. The Keep was not."

    06 — Fungal Chasms (The Violet Ravine)

    > "Day eighty-one. The Chasms echo. Every sound comes back wrong — louder, closer, as if the canyon is answering. A radio wedged between shelf-mushrooms played a voice I know: my own, recorded weeks ago, saying *follow the miasma downhill.* I did. The miasma led me to a door. The door was sealed. The door is still sealed. I am standing in front of it."

    07 — Glacial Cinder Peaks (The Black Ice)

    > "Day eighty-eight. The Peaks are silent except for the wind, which sounds like a choir. A radio frozen into a monolith played a final broadcast: *the bunker is where the ice is thinnest and the sky is closest.* I climbed. At the summit, the ice was thin enough to see through. Below it, a light. The bunker is under the ice. I am going down. If you are reading this, I did not come back."

  • *Bunker Location (pieced from clues):** Southwest of the Seat, 7°14′22″ south, ninety degrees east of the pole, where lightning refuses to strike, past the lying mirage, following the miasma downhill, under the thinnest ice at the summit — a pre-collapse vault buried beneath the Glacial Cinder Peaks, reachable only by drilling through the ice.
  • --

    • Part II — Bestiary Field Entries

    The Resonant (Strata Horror — Layer 2/3)

    > **Discovery trigger:** `sight_monster:resonant` or `mine_stratum:2`

    > I heard it before I saw it. A low, wet thrum in the basalt — not the singing of ore veins, which is almost musical, but something baser, hungrier. The Resonant is blind. It has no eyes, no face, only a pale elongated skull split open along the top where the sound gets in. Its limbs are too long and too many, and they move in a rhythm that matches the vibration it is tracking.

    > It does not see you. It does not smell you. It hears the Bulwark's reactor. It hears the drill. It hears your boots on stone. Stand perfectly still and it will walk past you, its head swaying like a tuning fork. Power down the mech and it loses interest within four seconds.

    > But do not think silence saves you. The moment you move — the moment you breathe too hard, the moment your jacket brushes the wall — it turns. And it does not stop.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** The Resonant's skull is split along the crown like a flower. The inside is dark. The inside is listening.

    The Drowned Maw (Tidal Abyssal Horror — Sunken Abyssal Sphere)

    > **Discovery trigger:** `sight_monster:drowned_maw`

    > It waits in the water. That is the first thing to understand. The Drowned Maw does not hunt on land; it hunts in the shallows, half-submerged, its jaw open and flat against the seabed like a trapdoor. You will see it only if you are looking for it, and you will only be looking for it if you have already lost someone to it.

    > The jaw is enormous — wider than a Bulwark — and lined with teeth that are not teeth but broken anchors, rusted and sharp. When it closes, the sound is not a snap. It is a gulp. The water takes everything in, and the Maw takes the water.

    > On the Sunken Abyssal Sphere, the tide is the Maw's ally. At high tide, the shallows flood, and the Maw rises. At low tide, it is stranded, half-buried in mud, its jaw gaping at the sky. That is when you kill it. That is the only time you kill it. Do not approach at high tide. Do not approach at high tide. Do not approach at high tide.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** The Maw's jaw, open, seen from above — a dark circle in the water with teeth like a broken crown. The eye is not visible. There is no eye.

    The Core Spire Anchors & The Four-Note Chord ("The Choir Beneath")

    > **Discovery trigger:** `mine_stratum:2` or `reach_core`

    > The Core City hums. I do not mean it makes noise — I mean it *hums*, the way a bell hums after it has been struck, except the bell has not been struck and the humming never stops. The four Crystalline Spire Anchors are the source. Each one sings a single note, and the four notes together form a chord that I could not name but that I felt in my sternum.

    > The chord is not music. It is a lock. The Autarch built it into the planet's architecture — four notes, four anchors, four keys. Shatter them in the wrong order and the Heart heals. Shatter them in the right order and the Heart dies. The right order is not written anywhere. It is only heard.

    > Stand near an anchor and listen. The note it sings is either resolving or discordant. Resolving means it is next in the sequence. Discordant means it is not. I stood at each anchor for an hour, listening, and I believe I have the order. I will not write it here. If the Autarch finds this journal, the order dies with me.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** Four spires arranged around the Heart Citadel, each emitting a glowing sound-wave. The chord is drawn as a musical staff with four notes, one per spire, in the correct order — but the order is left blank for the player to fill in.

  • --

    • Part III — Structure & World Spreads

    The Echo Wells ("The Singing Stone")

    > **Discovery trigger:** `phenomenon:echo_well` or `interact:echo_well`

    > The ground sings. Not everywhere — only where the basalt is thin and the ore veins run close to the surface. You will hear it as a low drone, felt more in the chest than the ears, like a heartbeat that is not yours. The Singing Basalt fissures are the source: cracks in the earth where the crystal veins are exposed, humming with a frequency that makes the pebbles dance.

    > The Echo Wells are older than the singing. They are circular basalt cisterns, half-buried, lined with acoustic rings that glow faintly cyan-magenta. Drop a Resonance Charge down the shaft and the sound ripples outward — a sonar thrum that paints the nearest Core Borehole Shaft on your map like a compass bearing drawn in light.

    > But the sound travels both ways. The Autarch hears it. The Stalkers hear it. The price of knowing where the Core is, is announcing that you want to go there.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** An Echo Well ruin — circular basalt cistern, glowing acoustic rings, a Warlord dropping a charge. The sonar ripple expands outward, painting a compass bearing toward a distant Borehole Shaft.

    The Ashen Furnace ("The Furnace That Eats")

    > **Discovery trigger:** `build:ashen_furnace` or `event:furnace_overheat`

    > I found the first Furnace in a ruined factory block, half-buried in soot. It was still warm. The colonists who built it are gone — not dead, just gone, as if the Furnace consumed them along with the tithe they fed it. The iron is pitted with handprints. Small handprints. Children's handprints.

    > The Furnace burns citizens. Not their bodies — their names. Feed it a citizen and the region's loyalty drops, but the Keep grows stronger, the towers hit harder, the walls repair themselves. It is a trade: one life for many. The colonists understand this trade. They do not resist it. They have learned that resistance is a language the Furnace does not speak.

    > But the Furnace has an appetite. Three citizens and it glows like a second sun. Four, and it screams. The iron splits, the soot ignites, and from the ashes a Brood-Mother crawls out, dragging her egg sacs through the wreckage of the base she was born from. The Furnace does not care whose base it is. The Furnace only knows hunger.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** The Ashen Furnace — dark soot-iron structure, glowing ember grate (amber → crimson-magenta at 3× stacks). A citizen silhouette being fed in. At 4×, the Furnace splits open and a Brood-Mother emerges from the flames.

    The Keep's Bell & The Curfew

    > **Discovery trigger:** `build:keep_bell` or `event:curfew`

    > The Bell was the first thing the colonists built. Before the Keep, before the walls, before the Shrine — the Bell. It rang at dawn and dusk, and the colonists came. They came because the Bell meant safety. They came because the Bell meant someone was watching.

    > Now the Bell rings for other reasons. Ring it and the colonists rally — they gather at the Keep, their loyalty steadies, the towers hum with borrowed courage. But ring it during an uprising and the mob turns. The Bell that called them to safety now calls them to the gate. The same sound, the same bronze, the opposite meaning.

    > At night, the colonists retreat. The huts close, the streets empty, the ash settles undisturbed. Unless a lamp burns near the Keep — then they stay. They work through the dark, their tithe flowing, their hands busy. But the light draws the Hollow Stalkers. The Stalkers do not fear the lamp; they are drawn to it, the way a moth is drawn to a flame, except the moth wants to warm itself and the Stalker wants to put it out.

    > The curfew is not a rule. It is a gamble. Light the lamp and you gain the night. Darken the Keep and you keep the dark at bay. You cannot have both.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** A Keep at night — dark huts, empty streets, ash settling. A street lamp burns near the Keep; citizens work in its amber pool. At the edge of the light, three glowing eyes watch from the dark.

    The Wounded Earth ("Where the Earth Remembers")

    > **Discovery trigger:** `phenomenon:wounded_earth` (walk within 5 m of a Haunted Site)

    > The earth remembers. That is the only way to say it. Every battle, every death, every detonation leaves a mark that does not fade. The scars are not decoration — they are wounds. The planet's crust is thin where the fighting was worst, and through those thin places you can hear the dead.

    > I walked through a field of craters near the East March. Three of them, within eight metres of each other. The ground hummed. Not the singing of ore veins — something lower, something that sounded like breathing. I knelt. The breathing was coming from below. I put my ear to the scarred earth and I heard them. Not words. Not screams. Just breathing. Slow, patient, patient breathing.

    > The Haunted Sites are the places where the fighting was so intense that the planet could not heal. The scars cluster, and the cluster breathes. Walk through it and you will hear the dead. Stay too long and the dead will hear you.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** Three craters clustered on the sphere's surface, dark and scarred. A Warlord kneeling at the edge of the largest, ear to the ground. Faint wisps of ink-mist rising from the scars. No monsters visible. The horror is the sound.

    The Last Light (Blood-Sky Eclipse & Ink-Stain Fog Creep)

    > **Discovery trigger:** `weather:blood_eclipse` or `weather:eclipse`

    > The Blood-Sky is not a sunset. It is a wound opening. When the Autarch's Wrath crests, the sky tears along a seam that was always there, and through the tear you can see the Eclipse Eye — vast, weeping, magenta, watching. The light it sheds is not light. It is a stain.

    > Under the Blood-Sky, the world contracts. Firelight shrinks. Shadows lengthen. The monsters' eyes brighten, as if they have been waiting for this. And the fog — the fog that you thought was merely weather — begins to creep. Not outward. Inward. Toward the light. Toward the Keep. Toward you.

    > The Ink-Stain is the fog remembering. Every tile you have explored, every inch of ground you have mapped, begins to darken. The parchment clouds return. The cartography fades. The map forgets what you learned, and the only way to remind it is to build, to watch, to stay.

    > A Keep holds the ink at bay. A Watchtower pushes it back. But nothing holds forever. The Blood-Sky does not want to destroy you. It wants you to forget. And forgetting, on Varn, is the same as dying.

    > **Callout note for illustration:** The Blood-Sky Eclipse — the sky torn open, the weeping magenta Eye watching. Below, a single burn-barrel, its light shrinking. The fog creeping inward, ink-dark, toward the light. A Keep in the distance, its parchment flag still flying, holding the line.

    GAMEPLAY LOOP

    > **Primary orientation:** [docs/GAMEPLAY_LOOP.md](GAMEPLAY_LOOP.md). Machine-readable form: `gameplay_loop` in [docs/archive/plan_index.json](archive/plan_index.json). SHIPPED = live in v1.0; PROPOSED = post-release plan only.

    > **Primary orientation doc.** Describes the loop that is **shipped in v1.0**, grounded in live code. Anything not yet implemented is explicitly **PROPOSED** (post-release plan) and is never described as shipped. Companion machine-readable form: `docs/archive/plan_index.json` → top-level `gameplay_loop`; rendered in the PLAN BOOK tab via `docs/PLAN_BOOK.md`.

  • *Legend:** **SHIPPED** = live in v1.0. **PROPOSED** = post-release plan only, not in the shipping build.
  • --

    • 1. The Loop (SHIPPED)

    Warlord — build, earn, expand, survive, break the Heart

    1. **Land and claim a home.** Each Warlord drops in with **100 Tithe** (`Config.START_TITHE`) and an auto-settled home Keep (`GameState.reset_season()` → `_settle_home`).

    2. **Build.** `B` opens the radial build wheel; `R` rotates; placement must be within **40 m** (`Config.BUILD_REACH`). Structures cost Tithe (`Structure.DEFS`); `M` calls a Bulwark for **150 Tithe** (`Config.MECH_COST`).

    3. **Earn.** `GameState.tick()` pays Tithe every tick per owned region: `citizens.tithe_rate(r) × factory/shrine/oath bonus × edict multiplier`. Loyalty drifts toward a target (90% with a shrine), so population and loyalty are the economy.

    4. **Expand.** Stand **alone** in a region for **6 s** — **10 s** for the Seat top terrace (`Config.CAPTURE_SECONDS` / `SEAT_CAPTURE_SECONDS`). Two Warlords present cancels the capture (`Game._tick_captures()`).

    5. **Survive the Autarch.** Wrath fills over time, faster when one Warlord leads (`Wrath.rate()` rubber-band). The host spends it on monsters (Hunter 10, Brood Spire 60, Ash Wraith 35), disasters (40), edicts (25 each) and the Reckoning (100) via `Powers.DEFS` and `Game.cast_power()`. The monster cap is 40 (`Config.MAX_MONSTERS`); deaths respawn after `Config.RESPAWN_SECONDS` — there is no player elimination.

    6. **Break the Heart.** The Core is guarded by **4 Spire Anchors** (600 HP each). Each hums one of four notes (110 / 138.59 / 164.81 / 196 Hz), permuted by planet seed. Destroy them **in ascending pitch order**: each correct anchor cracks one quarter of the barrier. A wrong note is a **discord** — progress resets, the Heart heals 15%, three Hunters spawn, and fallen anchors re-ignite after 20 s (`CoreState.damage_anchor()`).

    7. **Reach the Core.** With all four quarters cracked, the **4,000 HP Heart** can be damaged. At **10% HP** the **180 s Reckoning Clock** starts; at **0 HP** the planet is won (`CoreState.damage_heart()`). Victory splits SP and rolls the season into a reseeded world (`Game._award_victory()`, `Game.end_season()`).

    Autarch — watch, judge, spend, escalate

  • Observe the public `Game.view`; the Verdict grades each cast over a **15 s** window (`Game._judge_until`), producing STRUCK (refund) or WASTED.
  • Spend Wrath through the **nine power slots** (`slot_1`…`slot_9`, `Powers.ORDER`); the host also runs an automatic cast tick (`Game._tick_auto()`).
  • Escalate: edicts (no-building, double-tithe, frenzy), Wrath-driven monster waves, eclipse/discord events. **PROPOSED:** fuller deterministic arsenal rotation (Wave 86), two extra powers (Wave 155), private dossier tells (Waves 136/137/157).

    • Spectator — the broadcast

  • **SHIPPED:** `F` free camera, `1`–`8` follow a Warlord, `0` orbit (`SpectatorCamera._unhandled_input()`), with a live comparison card in `SpectatorHUD`.
  • **PROPOSED:** director pause `V` (Wave 59), commentary/bookmarks/lower third (Wave 100), odds board (Wave 49 + 152), beast-camera ride (Wave 149), tick trails (Wave 146).

    • 3. Win / Lose (SHIPPED)

  • **Warlord win:** reduce the Heart to 0 before the Reckoning Clock expires → planetary victory, SP split, epilogue, next season.
  • **Season loss for the Warlords:** the **180 s Reckoning Clock** runs out while the Heart still beats → `end_season()` without victory (`Game._core_events()` `"clock_end"`).
  • **Individual death is not elimination:** respawn, Keep loss and Bulwark loss are recoverable; the Autarch's win condition is the clock, not kills.
  • --

    • 4. First Five Minutes (SHIPPED ladder; captions partly broken)

    The shipped onboarding ladder is seven steps (`LoreFlavor.FIRST_TEN_VERBS`): **walk → wall → mine → stalker → burn_barrel → bulwark → raid_or_pact**, advanced by `Game._onboard_step()` with a 12 s guard and a 180 s auto-advance. Practical route:

    1. Move; find your home Keep and the nearby region borders.

    2. Build a cheap defensive structure (`B`, then `R` to rotate).

    3. Mine once (`T`) to learn the noise/depth system.

    4. Handle the first Hunter (fire with left mouse; sprint with `Shift`).

    5. Burn a barrel if one is nearby (`E`).

    6. Call the Bulwark (`M`) when Tithe allows.

    7. Raid a citizen or offer a pact (`E` / `P`).

    Completing the ladder records the Legacy epitaph **"The First Five Minutes."** **PROPOSED:** Wave 147 repairs the first-key captions, which currently fall through to random whispers for most verbs.

    • 5. Honest Gaps (not shipped)

  • **Underground is underdeveloped.** Mining is numeric noise plus sparse terrain deltas; the underground cutaway is described as dark/flat in `docs/QA/ART_QUALITY_AUDIT.md`. There is no fully explorable subterranean layer in v1.0. **PROPOSED:** depth gauge, cave-ins, cavity flags (Waves 104/162), echo wells (Wave 166).
  • **Autarch powers are weak.** `docs/BALANCE_AND_ECONOMY_SHEET.md` notes the Brood Spire is the only meaningful Wrath gate, everything else is affordable within 10–40 s, and the Brood is a bullet sponge a sprinting Warlord outruns. **PROPOSED:** better AI rotation and tells (Waves 86/102/155).
  • **The world is barren.** `docs/WORLD_CITIES_PLAN.md` describes Varn as "sparse greybox discs"; props are few and lighting is flat. **PROPOSED**: denser lived-in cities and atmosphere (World Cities plan), plus the many post-release prop/lighting waves in the Plan Book.
  • --

    • 6. Purpose of the Seat Pillar (SHIPPED object, no gameplay effect)

    The Seat at the north pole carries a **140 m energy shaft** (`WorldBuilder._seat()`, `beam_h := 140.0`) with a shadowless OmniLight and rising crystal motes. Its shipped purpose is **orientation and ceremony**: a horizon landmark visible across the curved sphere, and a faction-tinted **coronation marker** when the Seat changes hands (`Game.seat_coronation()` → `Art.set_faction()`).

  • *It currently has no gameplay effect** — it does not grant Tithe, Wrath, vision, protection or a win condition. **PROPOSED:** Wave 165 would faction-tint the shaft/motes and drive a capture intensity uniform; Wave 73 already tracks seat tenure as spire scars/reign counter; Wave 173 would place a hostage in the Seat cages. None of these change the pillar's shipped non-gameplay status.

    • VISUAL OVERHAUL

    > **Primary program doc:** [docs/VISUAL_OVERHAUL_PLAN.md](VISUAL_OVERHAUL_PLAN.md). Machine-readable form: `visual_overhaul` in [docs/archive/plan_index.json](archive/plan_index.json). POST-RELEASE / NON-BLOCKING. No gameplay code, no tags, no v1 readiness edits.

    > **POST-RELEASE / NON-BLOCKING PROGRAM.** Not a wave plan. The owner's verdict: *"graphics need a MAJOR overhaul, textures look flat and gross, buildings and placement of structures isn't natural or makes sense and clip into terrain, world just feels barren."* This program decomposes that verdict into four workstreams with measurable acceptance criteria and concrete existing-code hooks. **No gameplay code, no tags, no v1 readiness edits.** `[Autarch Idea Engine]`.

    0. Honest Scope

    This is large. The codebase already has a strong 3D pipeline (`world_builder.gd`, `strata.gd`, `SphereChunks`, `diorama_3d.gdshader`, `Art.*`), but the *art* and *placement* layers are underdeveloped: flat cel bands, greybox discs, sparse props, no terrain snap. Expect multiple waves / sprints, each gated by Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5 with before/after 52° + 40 m captures. **Do not fold into v1.0.** Treat each workstream as its own wave family so the Plan Book stays the single source of truth.

  • --

    • 1. Workstream 1 — Texture Depth

  • *Problem:** `docs/QA/ART_QUALITY_AUDIT.md` finds flat/dark surfaces with little weathered variation, hard black shadows, and "plastic" seams; the `diorama_3d.gdshader` already has `albedo_mul`, triplanar detail tiles, ground crack maps, `soot` grounding and `crystal_age` — but most materials don't use them.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `art/diorama_3d.gdshader` — `albedo_mul`, `albedo_tex`, `use_uv_albedo`, `ground_ash`/`ground_scrub`/`ground_mud`/`ground_basalt`/`ground_salt` samplers, `ground_metres`, `ground_crack_gamma`, `soot`, `fow` include.
  • `art/art.gd` — `toon()`, `faction()`, `glow()`, `part()`, `_omni()`, material cache keys.
  • `ui/ui_theme.gd` — `style_9s()`, `body_font()`.
  • `assets/textures/apoc/` — existing P/256 indexed textures (`decal_cracks`, `ground_ash_dirt`, `decal_maw_rupture`, etc.).
  • *Spec:**
  • Audit every world/facade/ground material against the 9.5 gate library (`docs/ACCEPTANCE_TEXTURES_UI.md`, `docs/QA/ASSET_CAPTURE.md`). Document which pass/fail.
  • Wire `albedo_mul` + triplanar detail tiles on all facade/ground materials; use the existing indexed textures, **no new texture budget explosion**.
  • Use `soot` grounding at building bases and `crystal_age` tint on crystal props (already authored, mostly unwired).
  • Roughness/height: where a material has a height map, drive normal via the existing `ground_crack_gamma`-style SDF; otherwise keep flat to avoid overdraw.
  • Ink/hatch layering: reuse the `decal_cracks`/`decal_maw_rupture` decals as world-space overlays, not per-actor textures.
  • Headless-safe; no new lights (`0` actor `OmniLight3D` rule from `PIVOT_3D_TOPDOWN_PLAN.md`).
  • *Acceptance:** Textures/UI Skeptic ≥ 9.5 on the 52° + 40 m capture set; no new textures; VRAM within 8 GB; `docs/QA/VISUAL_REGRESSION.md` baselines updated.
  • --

    • 2. Workstream 2 — Structure Placement

  • *Problem:** structures clip into terrain and sit unnaturally: `WorldBuilder` height sampling vs Dyson grid snapping vs footprint vs post-placement terraform edits.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `world/world_builder.gd` — `_prop()` `:234`, `_static_body()` `:169`, `_scatter()` `:140`, `_stand()`/`_offset()`, `_seat()` `:156`.
  • `bases/structure.gd` — `footprint()`, `anchor_for()`, `model_footprint()`.
  • `bases/build_rules.gd` — `check()`, `check_footprint()`.
  • `world/strata.gd` — `layer_of_radius()`, `cavity_flags()`, `deepest_cavity()`, `make_edit()`.
  • `world/terraform.gd` — `edits()`, `make_edit()`.
  • `game/game.gd` — `add_structure()` `:706`, `refresh_flags()` `:886`, `_tick_captures()` `:1323`, `request_build()` `:1853`.
  • `config.gd` — `BUILD_REACH := 40.0`, `PLANET_RADIUS`.
  • *Spec:**
  • Diagnose: audit `Structure.anchor_for()` vs `Planet.surface()` vs `Strata` deltas; find where post-terraform edits leave structures floating/sunk.
  • Host-authoritative **snap-to-surface** in `add_structure()` / `request_build()`: recompute the structure's anchor height from `Planet.surface(dir) + strata.deltas` at placement time; reject if the delta exceeds a tolerance.
  • `BuildRules.check()` gains a `terrain_fit` clause that refuses placement where the surface delta differs from the structure's footprint by more than a threshold.
  • **Preserve Seat/Core clearance** (`CoreCity.in_core()`, `SEAT_LIFT`) — never snap into the Seat plateau or Core cavity.
  • Terraform edits after placement must refresh structure transforms (`refresh_flags()` already exists) — extend it to re-snap.
  • **No new RPC**; all validation host-side; clients rebuild from the same host edit packets.
  • *Acceptance:** zero clip-into-terrain in 52° captures across all four archetypes; `check_footprint()` rejects bad placements; headless tests pass; no new RPC.
  • --

    • 3. Workstream 3 — World Density

  • *Problem:** `docs/WORLD_CITIES_PLAN.md` describes Varn as "sparse greybox discs"; props are few; lighting flat.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `world/world_builder.gd` — `_props()` `:293`, `_scatter()` `:140`, `_march_clutter()` `:409`, `_seat()` `:156`, `BATCH_PROPS` `:13`, `_prop()` `:234`.
  • `art/art.gd` — `model()`, `part()`, `toon()`, `glow()`, `faction()`.
  • `world/battle_scars.gd` — `count_in_region()` `:175`, scar density.
  • `world/citizen_crowd.gd` — `WALK_SPEED` `:16`, sphere snap `:5`.
  • `world/fog_of_war.gd` — `state_at()` gating.
  • `Config.PLANET_RADIUS`, seeded RNG pattern (`rng.randf_range`).
  • *Spec:**
  • Add procedural ruins/props/foliage/ash drifts using **existing pooled art** (`rubble_pile`, `twisted_tree_*`, `burnt_car`, `barricade_wire`, `dead_reeds`, `mire_roots`, `ruined_hab_block`, `overpass_ruin`, `boulder`, `ashen_furnace`).
  • Deterministic seeding from `planet_seed` + region index + season (Wave 127 season-age can dim/darken older ash).
  • Fog-gated: only render props in explored regions (`FogOfWar.state_at >= 1`).
  • Cap instance counts per biome; VRAM-aware (reuse existing meshes, no new textures/lights).
  • **No new mesh/light/gameplay** beyond existing art; cap total props within existing perf budget (150+ FPS / 8 GB VRAM).
  • *Acceptance:** denser worlds in 52° captures across all four archetypes; no FPS/VRAM regression; props deterministic from seed; fog-gated; headless-safe.
  • --

    • 4. Workstream 4 — Gate Plan

    Every visual change runs through **Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5** with before/after **52° + 40 m** captures, per `docs/ACCEPTANCE_TEXTURES_UI.md` and `docs/QA/ASSET_CAPTURE.md`:

  • Capture matrix: per-archetype (varn/abyssal/glass/mycelial) × per-workstream × (52° hero + 40 m perspective).
  • Skeptic sign-off required before merge; rejected art retained as `REJECTED` in `docs/archive/asset_shots.json` (per current policy).
  • **No AI-generated art**; any new art must be live Dithershop (`docs/archive/asset_shots.json` capture_policy).
  • Visual regression baselines updated in `docs/QA/VISUAL_REGRESSION.md` / `docs/QA/VISUAL_BASELINES.md`.
  • Headless run completes with zero errors; `tests/unit.gd` assertions added per workstream.
  • --

    • 5. Overlap Table

    | Piece | Owner | Visual Overhaul action |

    |---|---|---|

    | Horizon prism mesh / CAP 12 / fog gating | **Wave 30** | Reference only — no beacon changes. |

    | Factory smoke plume, rebuild bell, wall wounds | **Wave 89** | Reference only — drive the existing pool. |

    | Depth gauge, stratum name, cave-in | **Wave 104** | Reference only — no terrain rule changes. |

    | Foundry Row bonus, district economics | **Wave 132/159/160** | Reference only — no economy changes. |

    | Seat shaft/light/motes, capture intensity | **Wave 165** | Reference only — no coronation changes. |

    | Visual overhaul (texture depth, placement, density, gate) | **This program** | Add these four workstreams only. |

  • --

    • 6. Measurable Acceptance Criteria (program-level)

  • **Texture:** every world/facade/ground material either passes Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5 or has a documented fix; zero new textures beyond the existing indexed set.
  • **Placement:** 0 clip-into-terrain instances in 52° captures across all four archetypes; `check_footprint()` rejects bad placements; headless tests pass.
  • **Density:** prop count within existing perf budget (150+ FPS / 8 GB VRAM); deterministic from seed; fog-gated; no new lights.
  • **Gate:** every workstream lands with before/after 52° + 40 m captures and Skeptic sign-off; no v1 readiness edits; no release tag.
  • --

    • 7. Suggested Sequencing

    1. Workstream 2 (placement) — fixes the most visible defect (clipping), unblocks density.

    2. Workstream 1 (texture depth) — makes existing surfaces read.

    3. Workstream 3 (density) — fills the barren world.

    4. Workstream 4 (gate) — runs continuously; each workstream lands through it.

    Each step should be its own wave family (e.g. `VISUAL_OVERHAUL_WS1_*`) so the Plan Book stays the single source of truth.

    GAMEPLAY LOOP

    Autarch — How the Game Is Actually Played

    · SHIPPED = live in v1.0. PROPOSED = post-release plan only, not in the shipping build.

    Warlord builds/earns/expands/survives, breaks four Spire Anchors in chord order, then the Heart; Autarch watches, judges and spends Wrath; Spectator broadcasts. No player elimination; the Reckoning Clock is the season-level loss.

    docs/GAMEPLAY_LOOP.md

    1. The Loop (SHIPPED)

    Warlord — build, earn, expand, survive, break the Heart

    1. **Land and claim a home.** Each Warlord drops in with **100 Tithe** (`Config.START_TITHE`) and an auto-settled home Keep (`GameState.reset_season()` → `_settle_home`).

    2. **Build.** `B` opens the radial build wheel; `R` rotates; placement must be within **40 m** (`Config.BUILD_REACH`). Structures cost Tithe (`Structure.DEFS`); `M` calls a Bulwark for **150 Tithe** (`Config.MECH_COST`).

    3. **Earn.** `GameState.tick()` pays Tithe every tick per owned region: `citizens.tithe_rate(r) × factory/shrine/oath bonus × edict multiplier`. Loyalty drifts toward a target (90% with a shrine), so population and loyalty are the economy.

    4. **Expand.** Stand **alone** in a region for **6 s** — **10 s** for the Seat top terrace (`Config.CAPTURE_SECONDS` / `SEAT_CAPTURE_SECONDS`). Two Warlords present cancels the capture (`Game._tick_captures()`).

    5. **Survive the Autarch.** Wrath fills over time, faster when one Warlord leads (`Wrath.rate()` rubber-band). The host spends it on monsters (Hunter 10, Brood Spire 60, Ash Wraith 35), disasters (40), edicts (25 each) and the Reckoning (100) via `Powers.DEFS` and `Game.cast_power()`. The monster cap is 40 (`Config.MAX_MONSTERS`); deaths respawn after `Config.RESPAWN_SECONDS` — there is no player elimination.

    6. **Break the Heart.** The Core is guarded by **4 Spire Anchors** (600 HP each). Each hums one of four notes (110 / 138.59 / 164.81 / 196 Hz), permuted by planet seed. Destroy them **in ascending pitch order**: each correct anchor cracks one quarter of the barrier. A wrong note is a **discord** — progress resets, the Heart heals 15%, three Hunters spawn, and fallen anchors re-ignite after 20 s (`CoreState.damage_anchor()`).

    7. **Reach the Core.** With all four quarters cracked, the **4,000 HP Heart** can be damaged. At **10% HP** the **180 s Reckoning Clock** starts; at **0 HP** the planet is won (`CoreState.damage_heart()`). Victory splits SP and rolls the season into a reseeded world (`Game._award_victory()`, `Game.end_season()`).

    Autarch — watch, judge, spend, escalate

  • Observe the public `Game.view`; the Verdict grades each cast over a **15 s** window (`Game._judge_until`), producing STRUCK (refund) or WASTED.
  • Spend Wrath through the **nine power slots** (`slot_1`…`slot_9`, `Powers.ORDER`); the host also runs an automatic cast tick (`Game._tick_auto()`).
  • Escalate: edicts (no-building, double-tithe, frenzy), Wrath-driven monster waves, eclipse/discord events. **PROPOSED:** fuller deterministic arsenal rotation (Wave 86), two extra powers (Wave 155), private dossier tells (Waves 136/137/157).

  • **PROPOSED:** director pause `V` (Wave 59), commentary/bookmarks/lower third (Wave 100), odds board (Wave 49 + 152), beast-camera ride (Wave 149), tick trails (Wave 146).

    • 3. Win / Lose (SHIPPED)

  • **Warlord win:** reduce the Heart to 0 before the Reckoning Clock expires → planetary victory, SP split, epilogue, next season.
  • **Season loss for the Warlords:** the **180 s Reckoning Clock** runs out while the Heart still beats → `end_season()` without victory (`Game._core_events()` `"clock_end"`).
  • **Individual death is not elimination:** respawn, Keep loss and Bulwark loss are recoverable; the Autarch's win condition is the clock, not kills.

    • 4. First Five Minutes (SHIPPED ladder; captions partly broken)

    The shipped onboarding ladder is seven steps (`LoreFlavor.FIRST_TEN_VERBS`): **walk → wall → mine → stalker → burn_barrel → bulwark → raid_or_pact**, advanced by `Game._onboard_step()` with a 12 s guard and a 180 s auto-advance. Practical route:

    1. Move; find your home Keep and the nearby region borders.

    2. Build a cheap defensive structure (`B`, then `R` to rotate).

    3. Mine once (`T`) to learn the noise/depth system.

    4. Handle the first Hunter (fire with left mouse; sprint with `Shift`).

    5. Burn a barrel if one is nearby (`E`).

    6. Call the Bulwark (`M`) when Tithe allows.

    7. Raid a citizen or offer a pact (`E` / `P`).

    Completing the ladder records the Legacy epitaph **"The First Five Minutes."** **PROPOSED:** Wave 147 repairs the first-key captions, which currently fall through to random whispers for most verbs.

    • CONTENT GAP

    5. Honest Gaps (not shipped)

  • **Underground is underdeveloped.** Mining is numeric noise plus sparse terrain deltas; the underground cutaway is described as dark/flat in `docs/QA/ART_QUALITY_AUDIT.md`. There is no fully explorable subterranean layer in v1.0. **PROPOSED:** depth gauge, cave-ins, cavity flags (Waves 104/162), echo wells (Wave 166).
  • **Autarch powers are weak.** `docs/BALANCE_AND_ECONOMY_SHEET.md` notes the Brood Spire is the only meaningful Wrath gate, everything else is affordable within 10–40 s, and the Brood is a bullet sponge a sprinting Warlord outruns. **PROPOSED:** better AI rotation and tells (Waves 86/102/155).
  • **The world is barren.** `docs/WORLD_CITIES_PLAN.md` describes Varn as "sparse greybox discs"; props are few and lighting is flat. **PROPOSED**: denser lived-in cities and atmosphere (World Cities plan), plus the many post-release prop/lighting waves in the Plan Book.

    • 6. Purpose of the Seat Pillar (SHIPPED object, no gameplay effect)

    The Seat at the north pole carries a **140 m energy shaft** (`WorldBuilder._seat()`, `beam_h := 140.0`) with a shadowless OmniLight and rising crystal motes. Its shipped purpose is **orientation and ceremony**: a horizon landmark visible across the curved sphere, and a faction-tinted **coronation marker** when the Seat changes hands (`Game.seat_coronation()` → `Art.set_faction()`).

  • *It currently has no gameplay effect** — it does not grant Tithe, Wrath, vision, protection or a win condition. **PROPOSED:** Wave 165 would faction-tint the shaft/motes and drive a capture intensity uniform; Wave 73 already tracks seat tenure as spire scars/reign counter; Wave 173 would place a hostage in the Seat cages. None of these change the pillar's shipped non-gameplay status.

    • VISUAL OVERHAUL

    Autarch — Visual Overhaul Program

    POST-RELEASE / NON-BLOCKING PROGRAM · PROPOSED = post-release program, not in the shipping build. Each workstream lands as its own wave family so the Plan Book stays the single source of truth.

    Owner verdict: graphics need a MAJOR overhaul — flat/gross textures, structures clipping into terrain and sitting unnaturally, barren world. Four workstreams: texture depth, structure placement, world density, gate plan. No gameplay code, no tags, no v1 readiness edits.

    docs/VISUAL_OVERHAUL_PLAN.md

    0. Honest Scope

    This is large. The codebase already has a strong 3D pipeline (`world_builder.gd`, `strata.gd`, `SphereChunks`, `diorama_3d.gdshader`, `Art.*`), but the *art* and *placement* layers are underdeveloped: flat cel bands, greybox discs, sparse props, no terrain snap. Expect multiple waves / sprints, each gated by Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5 with before/after 52° + 40 m captures. **Do not fold into v1.0.** Treat each workstream as its own wave family so the Plan Book stays the single source of truth.

  • --

    • 1. Workstream 1 — Texture Depth

  • *Problem:** `docs/QA/ART_QUALITY_AUDIT.md` finds flat/dark surfaces with little weathered variation, hard black shadows, and "plastic" seams; the `diorama_3d.gdshader` already has `albedo_mul`, triplanar detail tiles, ground crack maps, `soot` grounding and `crystal_age` — but most materials don't use them.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `art/diorama_3d.gdshader` — `albedo_mul`, `albedo_tex`, `use_uv_albedo`, `ground_ash`/`ground_scrub`/`ground_mud`/`ground_basalt`/`ground_salt` samplers, `ground_metres`, `ground_crack_gamma`, `soot`, `fow` include.
  • `art/art.gd` — `toon()`, `faction()`, `glow()`, `part()`, `_omni()`, material cache keys.
  • `ui/ui_theme.gd` — `style_9s()`, `body_font()`.
  • `assets/textures/apoc/` — existing P/256 indexed textures (`decal_cracks`, `ground_ash_dirt`, `decal_maw_rupture`, etc.).
  • *Spec:**
  • Audit every world/facade/ground material against the 9.5 gate library (`docs/ACCEPTANCE_TEXTURES_UI.md`, `docs/QA/ASSET_CAPTURE.md`). Document which pass/fail.
  • Wire `albedo_mul` + triplanar detail tiles on all facade/ground materials; use the existing indexed textures, **no new texture budget explosion**.
  • Use `soot` grounding at building bases and `crystal_age` tint on crystal props (already authored, mostly unwired).
  • Roughness/height: where a material has a height map, drive normal via the existing `ground_crack_gamma`-style SDF; otherwise keep flat to avoid overdraw.
  • Ink/hatch layering: reuse the `decal_cracks`/`decal_maw_rupture` decals as world-space overlays, not per-actor textures.
  • Headless-safe; no new lights (`0` actor `OmniLight3D` rule from `PIVOT_3D_TOPDOWN_PLAN.md`).
  • *Acceptance:** Textures/UI Skeptic ≥ 9.5 on the 52° + 40 m capture set; no new textures; VRAM within 8 GB; `docs/QA/VISUAL_REGRESSION.md` baselines updated.
  • --

    • 2. Workstream 2 — Structure Placement

  • *Problem:** structures clip into terrain and sit unnaturally: `WorldBuilder` height sampling vs Dyson grid snapping vs footprint vs post-placement terraform edits.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `world/world_builder.gd` — `_prop()` `:234`, `_static_body()` `:169`, `_scatter()` `:140`, `_stand()`/`_offset()`, `_seat()` `:156`.
  • `bases/structure.gd` — `footprint()`, `anchor_for()`, `model_footprint()`.
  • `bases/build_rules.gd` — `check()`, `check_footprint()`.
  • `world/strata.gd` — `layer_of_radius()`, `cavity_flags()`, `deepest_cavity()`, `make_edit()`.
  • `world/terraform.gd` — `edits()`, `make_edit()`.
  • `game/game.gd` — `add_structure()` `:706`, `refresh_flags()` `:886`, `_tick_captures()` `:1323`, `request_build()` `:1853`.
  • `config.gd` — `BUILD_REACH := 40.0`, `PLANET_RADIUS`.
  • *Spec:**
  • Diagnose: audit `Structure.anchor_for()` vs `Planet.surface()` vs `Strata` deltas; find where post-terraform edits leave structures floating/sunk.
  • Host-authoritative **snap-to-surface** in `add_structure()` / `request_build()`: recompute the structure's anchor height from `Planet.surface(dir) + strata.deltas` at placement time; reject if the delta exceeds a tolerance.
  • `BuildRules.check()` gains a `terrain_fit` clause that refuses placement where the surface delta differs from the structure's footprint by more than a threshold.
  • **Preserve Seat/Core clearance** (`CoreCity.in_core()`, `SEAT_LIFT`) — never snap into the Seat plateau or Core cavity.
  • Terraform edits after placement must refresh structure transforms (`refresh_flags()` already exists) — extend it to re-snap.
  • **No new RPC**; all validation host-side; clients rebuild from the same host edit packets.
  • *Acceptance:** zero clip-into-terrain in 52° captures across all four archetypes; `check_footprint()` rejects bad placements; headless tests pass; no new RPC.
  • --

    • 3. Workstream 3 — World Density

  • *Problem:** `docs/WORLD_CITIES_PLAN.md` describes Varn as "sparse greybox discs"; props are few; lighting flat.
  • *Hooks (existing):**
  • `world/world_builder.gd` — `_props()` `:293`, `_scatter()` `:140`, `_march_clutter()` `:409`, `_seat()` `:156`, `BATCH_PROPS` `:13`, `_prop()` `:234`.
  • `art/art.gd` — `model()`, `part()`, `toon()`, `glow()`, `faction()`.
  • `world/battle_scars.gd` — `count_in_region()` `:175`, scar density.
  • `world/citizen_crowd.gd` — `WALK_SPEED` `:16`, sphere snap `:5`.
  • `world/fog_of_war.gd` — `state_at()` gating.
  • `Config.PLANET_RADIUS`, seeded RNG pattern (`rng.randf_range`).
  • *Spec:**
  • Add procedural ruins/props/foliage/ash drifts using **existing pooled art** (`rubble_pile`, `twisted_tree_*`, `burnt_car`, `barricade_wire`, `dead_reeds`, `mire_roots`, `ruined_hab_block`, `overpass_ruin`, `boulder`, `ashen_furnace`).
  • Deterministic seeding from `planet_seed` + region index + season (Wave 127 season-age can dim/darken older ash).
  • Fog-gated: only render props in explored regions (`FogOfWar.state_at >= 1`).
  • Cap instance counts per biome; VRAM-aware (reuse existing meshes, no new textures/lights).
  • **No new mesh/light/gameplay** beyond existing art; cap total props within existing perf budget (150+ FPS / 8 GB VRAM).
  • *Acceptance:** denser worlds in 52° captures across all four archetypes; no FPS/VRAM regression; props deterministic from seed; fog-gated; headless-safe.

    • 4. Workstream 4 — Gate Plan

    Every visual change runs through **Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5** with before/after **52° + 40 m** captures, per `docs/ACCEPTANCE_TEXTURES_UI.md` and `docs/QA/ASSET_CAPTURE.md`:

  • Capture matrix: per-archetype (varn/abyssal/glass/mycelial) × per-workstream × (52° hero + 40 m perspective).
  • Skeptic sign-off required before merge; rejected art retained as `REJECTED` in `docs/archive/asset_shots.json` (per current policy).
  • **No AI-generated art**; any new art must be live Dithershop (`docs/archive/asset_shots.json` capture_policy).
  • Visual regression baselines updated in `docs/QA/VISUAL_REGRESSION.md` / `docs/QA/VISUAL_BASELINES.md`.
  • Headless run completes with zero errors; `tests/unit.gd` assertions added per workstream.

    • 6. Measurable Acceptance Criteria (program-level)

  • **Texture:** every world/facade/ground material either passes Textures/UI Skeptic 9.5 or has a documented fix; zero new textures beyond the existing indexed set.
  • **Placement:** 0 clip-into-terrain instances in 52° captures across all four archetypes; `check_footprint()` rejects bad placements; headless tests pass.
  • **Density:** prop count within existing perf budget (150+ FPS / 8 GB VRAM); deterministic from seed; fog-gated; no new lights.
  • **Gate:** every workstream lands with before/after 52° + 40 m captures and Skeptic sign-off; no v1 readiness edits; no release tag.
  • --

    • 7. Suggested Sequencing

    1. Workstream 2 (placement) — fixes the most visible defect (clipping), unblocks density.

    2. Workstream 1 (texture depth) — makes existing surfaces read.

    3. Workstream 3 (density) — fills the barren world.

    4. Workstream 4 (gate) — runs continuously; each workstream lands through it.

    Each step should be its own wave family (e.g. `VISUAL_OVERHAUL_WS1_*`) so the Plan Book stays the single source of truth.
